correctness.rationale: The fixed coordinate unitary gives A_{a,d}=r M_{exp(−dy)} V_a, d=δ, with boundedness exactly d≥0. The adjoint multiplier is r exp(−dy/a) composed with V_a* in the corresponding order, and the polar modulus is r M_{exp(−dy/a)}. This gives d→dq under the transform and W_c^*A_{a,d}W_c=A_{a,d/c}. For fixed 0<η≤1 and d>0, q crosses one at a=1. Dominated convergence applies to both multipliers on the operator and adjoint sides, but essential suprema give exact nonzero distances to the limits. Maximizing |exp(−qz)−exp(−z)| at z=log(q)/(q−1) gives the successive gap. Conjugating again to logarithmic translations gives weighted shifts whose two tails tend to one and zero. An interior eigen-recurrence decays at both tails in the stated operator or adjoint orientation; normalized measurable fields of solutions multiplied by arbitrary square-integrable scalar functions give infinite multiplicity. At radius r the product of weights on the one-tail has positive limit, eliminating eigenvectors for both recurrences; truncated plane waves on that tail give approximate null vectors for the shifted operator, with the weight error uniform across a bounded fundamental interval. At zero both operators are injective and the weight approaching zero rules out closed range. The zero-damping Fourier multiplier and a=1 multiplication cases have the stated boundary behavior. The commutator multiplier a^{-1}(exp(−2dy/a)−exp(−2dy)) gives the sign and claimed maximum directly.
residual_risks: Finite truncated-shift diagnostics cannot establish any infinite-dimensional spectral conclusion; the judgment uses the recurrence and global direct-integral proof. Strict sign here does not mean uniformly bounded away from zero.

evidence: The affine-index definition contains x^n→x^{an+b}. The Laplace transform sends A_{a,d} to a^{-1}C_{(z+d)/a} on the right half-plane Hardy space. A rotation sends this symbol to τ(w)=w/a+id/a on the upper half-plane; positive scaling normalizes its additive parameter. Schröderus Theorems 4.3–4.4 (Hardy index α=−1) establish matching disks and interior infinite-dimensional eigenspaces, for the operator in the expansive symbol case and the adjoint in the contractive symbol case.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This is genuine coverage of the disk, essential disk and interior eigenspace statements after scalar normalization, not a resemblance of spectral shapes. The affine family and its static spectrum are not the novel unitary Aluthge dynamics. The spectral type proof in the record additionally verifies injectivity and continuous-spectrum endpoints in its own model.

value.rationale: This family gives a quantitative witness that an Aluthge orbit can retain its full unitary equivalence class and nonnormality at every finite step yet converge strongly-star to a normal operator. The two directions of dilation give opposite limiting mechanisms under the same parameter law, and the uniform exact norm separations make the topology distinction testable, beyond recovering the formerly known static spectra or one-step transform.
residual_risks: A family-level example, not a general convergence theorem; no value claim rests on the known static spectrum alone.
